milestone.title: Email validation function with tests
milestone.description: A Python function is_valid_email(address) for our signup form, with unit tests. It should accept normal addresses, reject obviously broken ones (no @, no domain, double dots, spaces inside), ignore surrounding whitespace, and return False for non-strings.

The tests actually check valid and invalid addresses

I've sent this back to the freelancer for changes; the 100.00 USD stays on hold.

The submitted test suite does not pass. I copied `email-validator-buggy.py` into the sandbox and ran it: 4 tests, 1 failure. `test_accepts_plain_addresses` fails on `first.last+tag@mail.example.org`, which the function rejects. The local-part character class `[A-Za-z0-9._%-]` leaves out `+`, so the "All tests pass" claim in the notes is wrong.

Criterion findings:
- **c1 (function delivered): met, 0.85.** `is_valid_email` exists and runs, but it rejects a normal address with `+`, which the brief's "accept normal addresses" requirement covers.
- **c2 (rejects no @ or no domain): met, 0.95.** `maya`, `maya@`, `@example.com`, `maya@example` and `maya@@example.com` all return False.
- **c3 (unit tests included): met, 0.9.** The file has an `IsValidEmailTest` class with four test methods.
- **c4 (tests check valid and invalid addresses): met, 0.7.** The tests do assert both valid and invalid inputs, but one of them fails when run. I gave moderate confidence because the suite as delivered does not pass.

The requested fix is to add `+` to the local-part character class, rerun, and include the passing output in the resubmission. I did not find other problems that need changing.

summary: The submission does not pass its own test suite: one of four tests fails, so the "All tests pass" claim is incorrect.
feedback:
1. Running `python3 email-validator-buggy.py` gives 4 tests, 1 failure. test_accepts_plain_addresses fails on is_valid_email("first.last+tag@mail.example.org"), which returns False. The local-part character class `[A-Za-z0-9._%-]` leaves out "+", which is a valid address character and is accepted by the brief's "accept normal addresses" requirement. Add "+" to the local-part character class (for example `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]`), then rerun and confirm all tests pass.
2. Please re-run the full test file and include the output (for example "Ran 4 tests ... OK") in your resubmission so the claim can be checked.
Everything else looks reasonable: the rejection cases (no @, no domain, double dots, inner spaces, non-strings) and whitespace trimming work as the tests describe. No other changes are required.
